title: Class Variable and Open Class State Leakage
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x; MRI — class-level state (@@vars, class instance variables) is shared across all threads and requests in the process
security_mechanism: Ruby classes are open: any code that loads can reopen a class and redefine a validation or authorization method, silently changing its semantics for the whole application without a call-site change. method_missing dispatch paths expose and route methods the class never declared, and send ignores private/protected visibility, so 'private' is not an access control against send callers. Class-level mutable state — @@class variables and class instance variables — is a single object shared by every request and thread, so per-user security state stored there (current user, ACL, CSRF material) leaks between concurrent requests: one user's authorization satisfies another's check.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent requests sharing process-global state; attacker-influenced dispatch names routed through method_missing/send.
source_sink_clues.sink: Reopening/monkey-patching of auth-relevant methods; method_missing dispatch without allowlist; send reaching private methods; @@class variables and class-level attributes holding per-request identity or authorization state

tracking_guards: Require per-request state to live in Thread.current/fiber-local storage or request-scoped objects, never @@variables; require respond_to_missing? paired with method_missing and an allowlist of routed names; require send targets validated against fixed allowlists; treat redefinition of security methods by loaded libraries as a change to review.
not_candidate_when: Class-level variables hold only immutable configuration written once at boot, method_missing routes a fixed allowlist and responds correctly to respond_to_missing?, and dispatched method names are allowlist-checked before send.
public_references: CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/470.html
CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
